title: Maximize Sum of Squares of Digits
summary: Given two positive integers num and sum, find a good integer n with exactly num digits and a digit sum of sum.
statement: Given two positive integers num and sum, find a good integer n with exactly num digits and a digit sum of sum. The score of n is the sum of the squares of its digits. Return the good integer with the maximum score, or an empty string if no such integer exists.
constraints: num is at most 200,000 and sum at most two million.
Return an exactly num-digit positive integer whose digits total sum.
Maximize the sum of squared digits, breaking score ties toward the numerically largest integer; return empty when impossible.
hints: For a fixed digit sum, moving one unit from a smaller positive digit to a larger digit increases the square total.
Concentrate the sum into as many nines as possible, then one remainder, then zeros.
Place the largest digits first to obtain the largest integer among arrangements with the same maximal score.
The convex exchange argument forces this digit multiset, and feasibility is exactly sum≤9·num.
editorial: The convex exchange argument forces this digit multiset, and feasibility is exactly sum≤9·num.

tests.explanation: Concentrating the sum in the leading digit gives 30 with score nine.
Digits nine and eight maximize the score, and 98 is the larger tied arrangement.
